headline: EQUINOX GOLD VALENTINE MINOTAUR: AI-SUPPORTED DISCOVERY 8KM FROM MILL — 700M STRIKE OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS, GRAB SAMPLES TO 650 G/T AU
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) reported September 29 that its newly identified Minotaur Zone at Valentine, Newfoundland — located 8 kilometres from the operating mill and outside the main Valentine Lake Shear Zone — has been defined over a 700-metre strike length with mineralisation open in all directions, surface grab samples grading as high as 650 g/t Au, and early step-out drilling suggesting a 2km potential system. Separately, the Musselwhite Mine in Ontario's PQ Extension Zone returned 22.9 metres averaging 10.00 g/t Au, confirming gold continuity up to 2km beyond current operations. The AI-assisted target generation at Minotaur, coupled with the bonanza-grade Musselwhite intercept, underscores district-scale exploration upside across Equinox's three Canadian gold mines just two weeks after the company outlined its 2M oz/yr production roadmap at Mining Forum Americas.

headline: UEC FISCAL 2026 ANNUAL RESULTS: Q4 PRODUCTION +157% TO 82,744 LBS — $93.13/LB REALIZED PRICE LEADS ALL PUBLIC URANIUM PRODUCERS
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE: UEC) reported its fiscal year 2026 full-year results on September 29: fourth-quarter production from Christensen Ranch and Burke Hollow totalled 82,744 pounds, up 157% from Q3's 32,195 pounds, as UEC's Texas ISR operations hit stride. Full-year production was 229,294 pounds at a total cost of $39.94/lb. The company sold 400,000 pounds from physical inventory at a weighted-average realized price of $93.13/lb — which the company states is the highest realized price among publicly traded uranium producers — generating $37.3 million in revenue and $16.9 million in gross profit for fiscal 2026. Liquid assets stand at $753 million (cash $495 million), with no debt. For retail investors tracking domestic uranium ISR producers, UEC has now fully transitioned from a single-mine operator to a multi-mine producer with a high-premium physical uranium monetisation strategy.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER MINTO NORTH: 9.27% CU, 7.43 G/T AU, 54.9 G/T AG OVER 5.4M — BONANZA-GRADE HIT AS PHASE 2 PASSES 52,000M IN YUKON
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines (TSX-V: SCMI) announced September 29 that hole 26SCM209 at the Minto North target in Yukon returned 9.27% Cu, 7.43 g/t Au, and 54.9 g/t Ag over 5.4 metres — equivalent to 15.1% CuEq — at the southern margin of the 202 Lens. The intercept represents bonanza-grade polymetallic mineralisation in a step-out position at a resource area the company considers a priority expansion target. Selkirk's Phase 2 program has now drilled 52,485 metres in 224 holes, making it one of the largest active drill programs on a TSX Venture copper-gold explorer. The company is hosting an investor update on October 2, 2026, to present a recently completed Preliminary Economic Assessment and the initial Mineral Resource Estimate — the first formal valuation of the project since Selkirk assumed site responsibility from Pembridge Resources.

headline: GOLD AT 8-WEEK LOW OF $4,123 AS 70% OF MARKET PRICES AN OCTOBER RATE HIKE — BOUNCE ATTEMPT STALLS BELOW $4,150
snippet: Gold touched an eight-week low of $4,123/oz in Asian trading on September 29, 2026 before recovering modestly to $4,150, but FXStreet analysts caution the bounce is fragile: CME Group's FedWatch Tool now puts a 70% probability on another 25bp rate hike at the October FOMC meeting, the US dollar is near a two-month high, and Treasury yields remain elevated after the Fed's September hike — its first in more than three years. Key near-term resistance is $4,185 and then $4,227; a daily close below $4,100 would open the door to the 50-day moving average near $4,050. Silver is trading at $60.80/oz, still holding the critical support level identified in Heraeus's September 28 analysis as the threshold whose breach would accelerate the precious metals correction.

headline: BRIXTON METALS THORN: 58M AT 0.50 G/T AUEQ AND 17.6M AT 1.47 G/T AUEQ IN GLENFIDDICH ZONE — RESOURCE ESTIMATE COMMENCES AT BC CAMP CREEK
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSX-V: BBB) released final drill results from the Camp Creek high-sulphidation target at its Thorn Project in northwest British Columbia on September 29, with the Glenfiddich Zone returning 58.0 metres at 0.50 g/t AuEq and a higher-grade internal interval of 17.6 metres at 1.47 g/t AuEq. The company has now commenced work on a Mineral Resource Estimate covering both the high-sulphidation Glenfiddich Zone and the underlying Camp Creek porphyry system, with the MRE expected in Q1 2027. The transition from drill results to a formal resource estimate is a significant milestone for a TSX Venture explorer; Thorn has not previously had a NI 43-101 compliant resource. For TSXV-focused investors, the Q1 2027 resource is the primary near-term catalyst.

headline: B2GOLD GOOSE MINE: 170K-200K OZ 2026 GUIDANCE INTACT — MOBILE CRUSHER AT 3,000 TPD AND BACK RIVER DISTRICT DRILLS EXTENDING RESOURCES
snippet: B2Gold (TSX: BTO) reported September 28 that the Goose Mine in Nunavut remains on track to deliver 170,000 to 200,000 ounces of gold in 2026, with mobile crushing exceeding 3,000 tonnes per day since mid-August and fixed plant crushing expected to reach a sustained 3,200 tpd in October following Phase 1 repairs to fire-damage. The Back River Gold District exploration program continues to extend the resource base beyond Goose's current Indicated Resource of 3.79 Moz at 7.40 g/t Au. For investors tracking B2Gold's Arctic pivot, the combination of operational recovery and ongoing district-scale exploration at one of the world's highest-grade development mines reinforces the bull case at current gold prices above $4,100/oz.

headline: COPPER TICKS UP AS ESCONDIDA SUPERVISORS VOTE THROUGH SEPTEMBER 30 AND CENTINELA MEDIATION CREATES TWIN SUPPLY RISK IN CHILE
snippet: Copper edged 0.15% higher to $6.56/lb on September 29 as markets priced in potential disruption from two of Chile's largest mines: the Sindicato N°2 supervisors' union at BHP's Escondida (1.2 Mtpa) is conducting its strike vote September 28-30, having unanimously rejected BHP's final contract offer, while workers at Antofagasta's Centinela (290 Ktpa) have already voted 98.73% for a strike and entered mandatory government-led mediation. Both dispute outcomes remain unresolved, creating a scenario where two mines that together produce roughly 12% of Chilean copper output could face work stoppages simultaneously. The $6.56/lb COMEX price is still 35% above year-ago levels but has pulled back 4% from September's record high above $6.83/lb as macro headwinds from Fed rate hike expectations weigh.

headline: GOLD HUNTER GREAT NORTHERN: 2,879M DRILLED IN 13 HOLES — PROGRAM ENDS SHORT AS BRIDGE SAFETY DEFECT DEFERS THOR DEPOSIT TO 2027
snippet: Gold Hunter Resources (CSE: HUNT) concluded its 2026 drill program at the Great Northern Project in Newfoundland on September 28, drilling 2,879 metres in 13 holes across six target areas including Kramer, Simms Ridge, and Incinerator — far short of the planned 10,000 metres. Drilling ended when expenditures reached the program budget, with per-metre costs substantially higher than estimated due to scope changes. More significantly, drilling at the high-priority Thor Deposit was deferred entirely to 2027 because of unanticipated safety problems with a bridge on the access road, pending a repair permit. The development is a setback for a CSE junior that had positioned the Thor Deposit as its primary 2026 catalyst; the programme conclusion without assay-stage results from Thor means investors will wait at least until early 2027 for the key data.

headline: FED'S FIRST RATE HIKE IN THREE YEARS RESETS THE GOLD BULL CASE — WHY $4,100 IS THE MAKE-OR-BREAK LEVEL FOR JUNIOR MINERS THIS QUARTER
snippet: Capital.com's September 29 analysis argues that the Fed's September 2026 rate hike — its first in over three years — does not end the gold bull market but does fundamentally reset its timeline and risk profile. With 70% of the market now pricing in a second hike in October, the analysis identifies $4,100/oz as the pivot level below which institutional gold positioning would face forced liquidation from rate-sensitive long ETF holders. Junior gold miners carry additional risk: at $4,100 spot, operating margins remain strong, but at $3,900 — the level a 50bp total tightening could theoretically pressure gold toward — several mid-tier developers with all-in sustaining costs above $1,800/oz would see significant project economics compression. The piece argues the key variable is whether October NFP and PCE data validate further Fed action, and recommends investors focus on funded developers rather than pre-resource explorers during the current period of elevated macro uncertainty.

headline: LITHIUM EQUITIES EXTEND SELLOFF AS YIELDS RISE — ALBEMARLE DOWN 2.1%, SQM DOWN 2.6% AS FED HIKE BETS PRESSURE BATTERY METALS
snippet: Lithium mining equities fell further on Tuesday September 29 as rising US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar made long-duration battery metals stories less attractive: Albemarle (NYSE: ALB) lost 2.1% and SQM (NYSE: SQM) fell 2.6%, with the LIT ETF down a further 1.3%, extending Monday's selloff triggered by the 5% crash in Chinese lithium carbonate to 126,350 CNY/T. The equity decline comes despite Albemarle reporting an average realised lithium price of US$19.53/kg of LCE in Q2 2026 — up 60.5% year-over-year — underlining the disconnect between improving fundamentals for established producers and the macro rate-driven sell pressure on the sector. For TSX-V and ASX junior lithium developers, the combined pressure of a structurally fragile commodity floor near $18,800/T LCE and rising discount rates is compressing valuations on projects that require $25,000–$30,000/T prices to achieve economic feasibility.
